To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HPC environments need to provide the ability to dynamically allocate resources to Hadoop/Spark applications; (2) Hadoop/Spark need to provide the capability to dynamically request resources from the HPC environment.
HPC and HDFS have complementary capabilities and can be combined in an efficient way to address scientific applications that need to couple traditional HPC compute stages with data analytics.
the integration of HPC and Apache Hadoop is possible, that there are multiple ways to do so, and that the choice of the integration strategy depends on the application and its requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a middleware for integrating HPC and HDFS.
the design and implementation of middleware that supports integrated use of Hadoop/Spark and HPC environments.
how best to couple Hadoop and HPC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed integration of Hadoop and Pilot-based dynamic resource management, and that the approach can be used to couple traditional high-performance computing stages (e.g., simulations) with Apache Hadoop based analysis.
the Hadoop ecosystem provides the best solution for the data analysis needs of many scientific domains.
the Hadoop and HPC ecosystems can be integrated and that the Pilot Abstraction provides an important unifying layer for this integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are providing a unifying resource abstraction layer that enables Hadoop applications to run on top of HPC environments.
we have developed a framework for integrating the HPC and HDFS worlds.
the integration of HPC and Big Data is possible and that the middleware presented here can be used to support the development of such applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of Hadoop and HPC is possible, but requires a deep understanding of the respective systems and their limitations, and the development of new middleware that supports the integration.
the integration of HPC and Apache Hadoop can provide a powerful platform for the next generation of scientific applications.
HPC and Hadoopy environments are not mutually exclusive.
